learning_outcomes.description: Plan and conduct research to inform the drafting, revision, and editing of creative writing or related projects, demonstrating ability to apply craft techniques and integrate developed ideas.
Analyse and evaluate practice and theory underpinning contemporary creative writing or related projects, including stylistic, structural and rhetorical strategies employed their production.

Investigate the ethical, creative, and professional challenges in the development and delivery of a new creative writing or related-project, demonstrating awareness of diverse perspectives, integrity, and social responsibility.
Assess significance of trends, debates and industry contexts that shape creative practice across a range of written forms.
Collaborate effectively in workshop settings through provision of constructive, discipline-specific feedback that demonstrates critical thinking and sensitivity to working with others.

assessments.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Practical/ Demonstration, Presentation, Reflection
assessments.task_description:
Through completion of a series of in-class tasks and activities, this assessment will enhance your understanding of the practice, processes and challenges of initiating, researching and developing new creative works.

Activities to be completed – outlined on LearnUQ – range from writing exercises, workshopping, and group discussion, which includes sharing exercises, works-in progress, and insights on craft, process and artefact development and submission. These activities will facilitate understanding and consideration of form, storytelling, elements of narrative, and broader issues and concerns including cultural difference, intersectionality and intercultural, ethical and relational communication.

Completion of in-class tasks and activities (between Weeks 4 to 12) will be awarded up to 8 points per class. Your best marks from five weekly tutorials will be added together to give you a final mark out of 30. Your mark should reflect a ‘meaningful contribution’, where it aids your own and the work of your peers, and or adds to, augments, the co-creation of knowledge and understanding.

While your best five tutorials will make up your final mark, we encourage you to participate in as many tutorials as you are able.

There are 8 opportunities across the semester, each worth 8%. Only your best 5 results count toward your mark (/40%) for the assessment. While there is flexibility to miss up to 3 sessions — for illness or any other reason — with no penalty and no documentation required, we would encourage you to attend as many seminars as possible.

There are no opportunities to re-take an individual exercise, and no alternative assessment is available except in the specific circumstances set out below. As this is an internal course, you must make yourself available to complete each exercise at the scheduled date, time and venue.

The writing activities are handwritten, closed-book tasks: no written material, electronic material or electronic devices may be used. All such items must remain in your bag or under your desk, and all electronic devices must be switched off or in airplane mode. If a device emits any noise, you may be subject to an allegation of misconduct and the item may be confiscated for the duration of the exercise. You may bring suitable writing implements (in a clear container), water in a clear bottle with the label removed, and disposable earplugs.

The discussion activities will be delivered during seminar and are also closed-book tasks: no written material, electronic material or electronic devices may be used. All such items must remain in your bag or under your desk, and all electronic devices must be switched off or in airplane mode. If a device emits any noise, you may be subject to an allegation of misconduct and the item may be confiscated for the duration of the exercise.

You will share 'workings' and reflections in class as you undertake written activities. Your mark will reflect a ‘meaningful contribution’ to class discussion. Your contribution is 'meaningful' where it adds to, augments, the co-creation of knowledge and understanding. This may include (but is not limited to): asking thoughtful and relevant questions; sharing appropriate and relevant responses or commentary; engaging in peer feedback; or assisting peers in their completion of assigned activities.

While your best five tutorials will make up your final mark, we encourage you to participate in as many tutorials as you are able.

assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.

assessments.task_description:
Write a short essay that critically assesses the form you intend to employ in the production of the creative work submitted for your final assessment. For example, if you intend to submit a folio of 'flash' fiction, you might consider the work of Lydia Davis and examine the impacts the form has on word choice and storytelling; if you intend to submit a new short story, you might consider essays by Poe, Carver or Moore; if you intend to submit a short comic or sequential art, you might consider drawing on the work of Scott McLoud; or if you intend to submit an excerpt from a longer piece of literary journalism, you might consider Tom Wolfe's influential discussion on the form, or examine its use in writing about climate crises or sport? You must consult with your tutor on the topic of your essay. Use citations with MLA style, include a reference list with at least 6 items.

To be submitted: Essay (1000 words (excluding refs))

assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
Write 2500 words of new original creative work or related project in your preferred form. Your submission should be based on your earlier examination of form, in-class discussion, and the research undertaken and resources sourced during your development of the piece. The work should be presented in standard manuscript format and if you wish, aligned to the submission guidelines of your intended publisher (which should be noted).

To be submitted: Creative Work (2500 words (excluding refs))
